thread:
emily: Quick one 1: employee changed from biweekly to monthly payroll on 3/1; they have an active 401(k) loan with payroll withholding schedule tied to biweekly. Will their loan payment amount/ schedule automatically adjust or do we need to update payroll to prevent under/overpayments?

rob-payroll: Good catch. Payroll systems usually prorate loan payments to match pay frequency, but only if loan setup uses "auto-adapt" flag. Do we know how the loan was originally configured?

dana-benefits: Benefits system shows loan ID L-9812 created 2024-07 with frequency=BIWEEKLY and auto_adapt=false. Recommend manual adjustment.

emily: Ugh. Employee noticed a smaller deduction this period. They expected same monthly dollar but spread differently. They prefer to keep the same monthly principal+interest.

liz-finance: If we want to keep same monthly cash flow, payroll needs to increase the per-paycheck amount for monthly runs. Because loan was set for biweekly, the per-paycheck amount was ~1/2 of biweekly schedule; switching to monthly without change reduces annual repayment and extends term. Need written authorization from employee for a new amortization schedule.

rob-payroll: Process: 1) Employee signs loan amendment confirming new payment amount and effective date 2) Payroll updates deduction code LOAN_401K with new per-pay amount and memo 3) Benefits/Recordkeeper to update outstanding balance and remaining term. Our deduction codes: ```CSV
code,description
LOAN_401K,active 401(k) loan repayment
``` 

dana-benefits: Recordkeeper BrightPlan accepts loan adjustment file type "LOAN_ADJ" with fields SSN, loan_id, new_payment_amount, effective_paydate, signed_employee_consent. We'll process and re-amortize.

emily: Can payroll do a catch-up deduction if employee prefers to keep original term (i.e., one-off additional amount this month to makeup shortfall)?

rob-payroll: Yes we can do an off-cycle one-time catch-up using code LOAN_ADJONCE. Need People Ops approval and employee written request. Off-cycle will be taxable-normal payroll processing won't change taxes besides normal withholding.

liz-finance: Also verify there are no plan rules blocking increased payments above max-per-paycheck limits. I'll confirm with BrightPlan and post back.

hr-bot: Reminder: attach updated loan amendment to the personnel file.

emily: Thanks all. Action: 1) I will get employee amendment signed today 2) Rob to queue LOAN_ADJ file once signed and coordinate off-cycle if requested 3) Liz to confirm plan limits. Close when recordkeeper confirms re-amortization.
